title: Stand up a Cognito user pool federating Google
description:
**Phase 2 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 0ab02c
- **Runs in parallel with:** b574a6, which shares no files with this
- **Unblocks:** 5f0c4c, 5558db

---
CDK per environment: UserPool, UserPoolIdentityProviderGoogle, and a public app client using authorization code with PKCE and no client secret. Custom auth domain auth-dev, auth-staging, auth. Publish pool id, client id, and domain to SSM under the existing web parameter prefix.

Use single-label names. The existing certificate in infra/lib/dns-stack.ts covers *.chattic.us, and a wildcard matches one label only, so auth.dev.chattic.us would need a new certificate and auth-dev.chattic.us does not.

Cognito authenticates and nothing else. Do not model organizations, membership, or roles as Cognito groups: they are global to the pool, they land in the token, and token claims go stale against the records that govern spending.

**Done when:** development is deployed and the authorize URL with identity_provider=Google lands on Google's consent screen and returns a code.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Adversarial review: one-way doors in this task.**

A user pool cannot be reshaped in place, and three of its settings are create-time only. Getting them wrong means replacing the pool, and replacing the pool changes every Cognito sub.

- **Case sensitivity is fixed at creation.** Create the pool case-insensitive. Google can return Email@ and email@ for the same human, and a case-sensitive pool will happily hold both as different users.
- **Never key anything on the Cognito sub.** Identity is keyed on verified email, deliberately, so that replacing the pool costs nothing. Do not let a sub leak into Membership, Invitation, or any log we later join on.
- **One pool user per provider.** If Apple is ever added, the same human arrives as a second pool user. Email-keyed identity absorbs that; a sub-keyed one does not.

Also confirm the app client issues refresh tokens with a lifetime we actually want, since 5558db depends on silent renew and the default is thirty days.

comments.text:
summary: Google sign-in is live and complete on development. Cognito user pool federating Google was built in #155 (CDK: UserPool + UserPoolIdentityProviderGoogle, PKCE auth-code app client, no client secret, selfSignUpEnabled false, Google-only — no Cognito password IdP), deployed as the named ChatticusAuth development stack with hosted UI at auth-dev.chattic.us. The authorize URL with identity_provider=Google returns 302 to accounts.google.com and the callback returns a code, satisfying the done-when.

Web wiring followed: #160 inlined NEXT_PUBLIC Cognito env at build time so the SPA could load config, #161 pointed OIDC discovery at the Cognito issuer, #157/#158/#159 wired the Google sign-in flow and CloudFront invalidation. End-to-end sign-in was then blocked by Cognito reporting email_verified=false on Google id_tokens; #165 mapped ProviderAttribute.GOOGLE_EMAIL_VERIFIED into the id_token, redeployed ChatticusAuth, and full Google sign-in + GET /me began returning 200. Identity is keyed on verified email, never on the Cognito sub, per the adversarial review.

The human owner has signed in to https://dev.chattic.us via Google many times since, including through the membership branching work (22f5bb). Done-when met: development is deployed and the Google authorize URL returns a code. Closing.
